title: Truthiness
summary: In Luau conditions, only nil and false count as false. 0, "", and {} are all TRUTHY — a constant source of surprises for people coming from other languages.

explanation.whatItIs: The rule deciding what passes an `if`: everything passes except the two dedicated 'negative' values — nil and false.
explanation.whyItExists: Lua chose minimalism: real booleans express falsehood; absence (nil) also fails. All data is presumed present-and-useful.
whenToUse: `if value then` as an existence check (non-nil)
`x or default` patterns — remembering false ALSO falls through
whenNotToUse: Expecting JS/C-style falsiness (0, "", empty → false) — it's not here
tips: Existence idiom: `if obj ~= nil then` == `if obj then`
Need 'value unless nil or false'? Use explicit comparisons
Boolean-ish flags: name them clearly; don't lean on truthiness for tri-state logic
commonMistakes: `if count then` when count can be 0 — 0 passes! Use `if count ~= nil then` or `> 0`
`x or default` replacing legitimate `false` values with the default
Porting JS habits: `if (!x)` thinking — use `not x`

examples.title: The surprises, demonstrated
examples.code:
if 0 then print("0 is truthy!") end          -- prints
if "" then print("empty string truthy!") end  -- prints
if {} then print("empty table truthy!") end   -- prints

if nil then else print("nil is falsy") end    -- prints
if false then else print("false is falsy") end -- prints

-- The or-default trap:
local function greet(enabled)
    local prefix = enabled or "??"   -- false → falls through to "??"!
    print(prefix)
end
greet(false)   --> "??"  (not what you wanted?)

-- Explicit version:
local function greetSafe(enabled)
    local prefix = if enabled == nil then "default" else tostring(enabled)
    print(prefix)
end
